thread:
maya: heads up — got reports of gRPC streams from hosted inference to model-pool getting stuck in-flight for ~20–40s yesterday evening. connections stay ESTABLISHED but no application data for the duration. :eyes:

peter: any pattern on client IPs / egress nodes?

maya: mostly from a handful of egress NATs in us-west-2. p95 token latency spikes, not a full disconnect.

maya: pasted relevant logs and a tcpdump excerpt: ```
# server side (ingress):
[INFO] stream id=5 recv WINDOW_UPDATE delta=0
[WARN] stream id=5 no DATA frames for 32s
# egress nat: conntrack: src=10.2.3.7:40001 -> dst=52.23.11.9:443 NAT-> 3.120.45.231:40001
# repeated mapping observed with different underlying sockets
```

infra-bot: alert: NAT ephemeral port usage > 85% on egress-pool-3 (last 5m).

derek: hmm looks like ephemeral ports are getting reused quickly. if two different internal sockets get NATed to same 4-tuple in short succession that could confuse connection tracking on some middleboxes. did you see any RSTs?

maya: not a lot of RSTs. more like idle stalls. tcp shows keepalives, but application-level h2 frames don't flow.

anya: could be ALB / proxy doing asymmetric timeouts. ALB idle timeout default 60s, envoy route/conn idle 30s in our config — mismatch can leave one side thinking stream is fine while the other closed backing TCP -> subtle stalls for multiplexed h2.

peter: also saw this pattern when NAT reused ports: the downstream proxy (we suspect a managed edge appliance) was dropping WINDOW_UPDATE/CONTINUATION frames intermittently when it detected what it thought were duplicate client IP:port pairs.

maya: attached a minimal repro command I used: ```
grpcurl -insecure -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -proto ./api.proto -H "x-cust-id: m-123" my-edge-host:443 inference.Service/Chat --reflect
# run 50 parallel clients from one node
```

sre-ops: can you run that against canary-edge-2 (same egress pool) but with --metadata keepalive=30 and with tcpdump on egress-nat? want to capture 4-tuple reuse timing.

maya: running now. initial capture shows two internal sockets with source ports 40005 and 40008 getting NATed to same external port 62005 within 12s. see excerpt: ```
10.2.3.7:40005 -> 3.120.45.231:62005
10.2.3.10:40008 -> 3.120.45.231:62005
```

derek: that is bad. some NAT implementations don't create unique mapping entries for socket tuples when ephemeral range is limited and kernel reuses ephemeral ports quickly. Combine that with long-lived h2 streams and you can get stream demux confusion in the proxy.

anya: mitigation options:
- expand ephemeral port range on egress nodes
- add source IP preservation (if available) so NAT mapping differs
- increase conntrack table size / timeout
- ensure ALB/envoy idle/keepalive values align (route/stream idle > LB idle)
- patch proxy to drop/reject when mapping collision detected (safer than silent stall)

peter: immediate test: bumped ephemeral range to 32768-65535 on a subset egress nodes and re-ran the 50-parallel test. stalls went away for that pool. :white_check_mark:

maya: can confirm — p95 latency back to normal for canary pool. longer-term we should still find root cause upstream (managed LB or cloud NAT behavior).

deploy-bot: created task INFRA-542: investigate edge NAT port reuse + proxy frame drop (assignee: derek).

derek: I'll scope kernel settings, conntrack metrics, and vendor NAT doc. also want to run a test to toggle HTTP/2 connection pooling at the proxy to see if multiplexing exacerbates it.

anya: assigning follow-ups:
- derek: deep dive + vendor ticket
- maya: run traffic simulation against vendor staging with NAT stress
- peter: audit our ALB/Envoy idle/keepalive alignment across regions

maya: one gotcha — when we increased ephemeral range we saw a small uptick in SNAT ptables entries memory usage; conntrack sized fine though. keep an eye on memory.

peter: for next deploy let's also add a short live-check that detects long-inactive h2 streams (>20s no DATA) and force-close them so we fail fast rather than stall. we should treat that as a graceful degradation toggle behind a flag.

sre-ops: I've scheduled a 30m firebreak window tomorrow 03:00 UTC to run a broader repro across all egress pools. tagging: @derek @maya @peter.

maya: thanks — will join. adding collected pcap and grpc logs to INFRA-542. :thumbsup:

peter: TL;DR — root cause likely NAT ephemeral port exhaustion/reuse causing mapping collisions -> edge proxy mis-handles H2 frame multiplexing -> streams stall. mitigations: ephemeral range, conntrack, keepalives/timeout alignment, fail-fast stream pruning.

maya: closing note — weird, useful to see this crop up only under medium concurrency (30–60 streams). low load fine, high load you'd see resets. medium load reproduces the silent stall which was the hardest to triage.

sre-ops: copy for postmortem. will include timeline + graphs in INFRA-542.
